answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because cipher only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any pearl approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
